newsitem.title: USA: Franchisor HFS' profits double in fourth quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Franchisor HFS' profits double in fourth quarter, year.

text.p: Real estate, hotel and car rental franchisor HFS Inc., which rode a wave of acquisitions last year, said Monday its profits more than doubled in the fourth quarter and in all of 1996.

HFS earned $46.9 million, or 33 cents a share, in the final quarter of last year, compared with $20.3 million, or $18 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Revenues jumped 120 percent to $249 million from $113 million.

"Fourth-quarter results, which represent our 17th consecutive record-breaking quarter since we became a public company in 1992, illustrate the continuing strength of our operating businesses, as well as the benefits derived from the acquisitions completed during the year," said HFS Chairman Henry Silverman.

The company is the nation's largest franchisor of hotels and residential real estate brokerage offices. It also owns Avis Inc., the world's second-largest rental car system, and Resort Condominiums International Inc., the largest provider of vacation timeshare exchanges worldwide.
It recently announced a definitive merger agreement with mortgage provider PHH Corp., expected to close in March, 1997.

For the year, Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS earned $169.6 million, or $1.29 per share, up from $79.7 million, or $73 cents a share, in 1995. Revenues last year rose 93 percent to $799 million from $413 million.

"Our real estate franchise business is performing exceptionally well as unit growth in our three franchise networks, together with higher same store sales, translates into increased earnings for HFS," Silverman said in a statement accompanying the results.

He said the company's lodging franchise business had opened more than 31,000 rooms over the past 12 months and added that Avis and Resort Condominiums "... should each be significant contributors to 1997 results."
HFS stock was 37.5 cents higher at $64.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
